# Folio Game Engine

> Text adventures rendered as point-and-click graphic adventures that run in a
> browser. A game is one `.folio` file. This document is the complete authoring
> spec: an agent that reads it should be able to produce a valid game without
> fetching anything else.

Schema: https://folio.games/schema/world-0.1.0.json
Manual: https://folio.games/docs/
Source: https://github.com/rdyplayerB/folio

## Before you start

Two things are worth knowing because they change how you should work.

1. **You cannot ship a broken game.** `folio validate` replays your walkthrough
   from a cold start and requires it to reach the ending. It also computes the
   dependency graph and rejects worlds with dead ends. Write the walkthrough as
   you build, not at the end.
2. **The vocabulary is closed.** Sixteen conditions, sixteen effects. There is no
   scripting and no escape hatch. If you find yourself wanting one, the answer is
   almost always a flag or a counter.

## The loop

```
npm i -g folio-engine
folio pack my-game/ my-game.folio     # assemble
folio validate my-game.folio          # check. do this constantly
folio play my-game.folio              # play in the terminal
folio info my-game.folio              # what is inside
folio profile my-game.folio           # measure its design shape
folio brief brief.json                # resolve the dials into targets
folio calibrate story.z3              # Path A only: derive a room map
```

`folio brief` takes the dials below. To scale a game to a source rather than to a
default, count the places the source actually visits and pass them:
`{"source": {"locations": 30}}`. A flat `"source.locations"` key is ignored.

## A game is a directory

```
my-game/
  manifest.json             required
  walkthrough.folioscript   required, the proof it can be finished
  brief.json                optional, what you were aiming for
  logic/world.json          required for logicType "world"
  presentation/*.js         optional, the pictures
```

### manifest.json

All seven fields are mandatory.

```json
{
  "id": "my-game",
  "title": "My Game",
  "author": "Name",
  "folioVersion": "0.1.0",
  "logicType": "world",
  "license": "MIT",
  "contentRating": "all-ages",
  "capabilities": ["darkness", "timed-events", "score"],
  "aiDisclosure": { "prose": "generated", "art": "none", "note": "Reviewed by a human." }
}
```

- `logicType`: `world` (you write the world) or `zmachine` (an existing story file)
- `contentRating`: `all-ages` | `teen` | `mature`
- `license`: SPDX id, or `unknown` (playable, not hostable)
- `capabilities`: any of `darkness`, `timed-events`, `combat`, `containers`,
  `npc-dialogue`, `multi-save`, `custom-verbs`, `sound`, `score`
- `aiDisclosure`: state precisely what was generated. Do not overclaim.

### walkthrough.folioscript

One command per line. `#` starts a comment. Runs cold, no state injection.

```
# reach the ending
north
take key
expect: room HALL
south
use cellar-door
expect: score 5
```

Assertions: `expect: room ID`, `expect: score N`, `expect: moves N`.
Failure line numbers count **commands**, not file lines.

## logic/world.json

```
{
  "meta":     { ... },   required
  "flags":    { ... },   optional, your named booleans
  "counters": { ... },   optional, your named integers
  "rooms":  [ ... ],   required
  "items":  [ ... ],   required, may be empty
  "actors": [ ... ],   optional
  "rules":  [ ... ],   optional
  "timers": [ ... ]    optional
}
```

### meta

- `start` (required): room id the player begins in
- `title`, `seed`
- `magicWords[]`: words no player would guess, offered as one-tap buttons on the
  on-screen keyboard. Presentation only; the logic never reads them.
- `defaults`: overrides for built-in responses. Keys:
  `blocked`, `dark`, `what`, `already`, `absent`, `fixed`, `taken`, `nothave`,
  `dropped`, `alreadyOpen`, `locked`, `empty`, `unknown`, `wait`, `plain`.
  `unknown` is the most-heard line in most games. Write it.

### rooms

`id` (required), `name`, `prose`, `dark`, `exits[]`, `variants[]`

`variants` is how a room changes once something has happened in it. Each is
`{ "if": [conditions], "prose": "..." }`, tried in order; the first whose
conditions all hold replaces `prose`.

```json
{ "id": "HALL", "prose": "The ogre is slumped in his chair, snoring.",
  "variants": [
    { "if": [{ "type": "flag", "flag": "awake" }],
      "prose": "The ogre is on his feet, and he has seen you." }
  ] }
```

### exits

One way only. A return journey is a second exit on the other room.

- `dir` (required): `NORTH SOUTH EAST WEST NE NW SE SW UP DOWN IN OUT`
- `to` (required): room id
- `condition`: blocked until it passes
- `door`: item id, blocked while that item is closed
- `hidden`: while blocked, vanish rather than show as blocked
- `blocked`: what to say when this way is closed. Without it every locked door in
  the game shares one sentence

Three states reach the compass: a room id (open), `false` (blocked but visible),
absent (nothing there).

### items

`id`, `location` (required), plus `name`, `description`, `roomProse`,
`attributes`, `fuel`.

`description` is what `LOOK` at the thing says. **`LOOK` with a noun is examine**,
so you do not need to hand-roll inspection as `USE` rules.

`location` is a room id, another item's id (inside a container), `"PLAYER"`, or
`"NOWHERE"`. `roomProse` appears in the room description until the item moves.

Attributes the engine understands: `TAKEBIT` (can be picked up), `LIGHTSOURCE`,
`ONBIT` (starts lit), `OPENBIT` (starts open), `TRANSPARENT` (see inside without
opening).

### actors

`id`, `location` (required), plus `name`, `description`, `hostile`, `attributes`.
A hostile actor in the room sets `fighting`, which you can read as a condition. It
does no harm by itself; the harm is a rule or a timer.

`location` is a room id, `"NOWHERE"` until they arrive, or **`"PLAYER"` to travel
with the player**. A companion at `"PLAYER"` is present in every room you enter, so
speaking to them works everywhere rather than hitting the absent default. Move
someone into or out of the party with `move-actor` to `"PLAYER"` or to a room.

### rules

The only place anything interesting happens.

```json
{
  "on": { "verb": "USE", "noun": "CELLAR-DOOR", "room": "PORCH" },
  "if": [ { "type": "carrying", "item": "KEY" } ],
  "do": [ { "type": "set-flag", "flag": "doorUnlocked", "value": true } ]
}
```

`on.enter` fires when the player **arrives** in that room instead of on a command:
a floor that gives way, an ambush, a door closing behind you. A rule with `enter`
is never matched by anything typed or clicked.

**A rule can match a direction, and it preempts the move.** `{"verb": "NORTH",
"room": "QUAY"}` runs instead of walking north, and if its conditions fail it falls
through to the exit as normal. That is the idiom for a gate that explains itself.

`on.second` is a second object, for pairings like using a key on a door. The board
asks the player for one whenever a rule pairs objects under that verb.

```json
{ "on": { "verb": "USE", "noun": "CELLAR-DOOR", "second": "KEY" },
  "do": [ { "type": "print", "text": "The key turns." } ] }
```

**A rule without `second` will never match a two-object command**, so write the
pairing above the single-object fallback and the fallback still answers a bare
`USE CELLAR-DOOR`.

**Rules are tried in array order and the first match wins.** Put the specific case
above the general one. A rule whose conditions fail does not block later rules, so
the standard shape is a guarded rule followed by an unguarded fallback for the same
trigger. That fallback is where the writing goes.

### conditions (all seventeen)

| type | fields | true when |
|---|---|---|
| `flag` | `flag`, `value` | flag equals value (default true) |
| `carrying` | `item` | player holds it |
| `in-room` | `item` | lying in the current room |
| `present` | `item` | carried or in the room |
| `at` | `room` | player is there |
| `visited` | `room` | player has been there |
| `open` | `item` | it is open |
| `lit` | `item` | it is alight |
| `score-at-least` | `value` | score >= value |
| `counter-at-least` | `counter`, `value` | counter >= value |
| `counter-equals` | `counter`, `value` | counter is exactly value |
| `actor-here` | `actor` | that actor is in this room |
| `fighting` | | a hostile actor shares the room |
| `chance` | `percent` | a roll off the seeded generator, default 50 |
| `not` | `condition` | nested condition is false |
| `all` | `conditions` | every one holds |
| `any` | `conditions` | at least one holds |

### effects (all sixteen)

| type | fields | does |
|---|---|---|
| `print` | `text` | adds a line to the response |
| `set-flag` | `flag`, `value` | sets a flag (default true) |
| `take` | `item` | move to player, ignoring TAKEBIT |
| `move-item` | `item`, `to` | to a room, `PLAYER`, a container, or `NOWHERE` |
| `destroy` | `item` | remove from play |
| `open` / `close` | `item` | mark open or closed |
| `light` / `extinguish` | `item` | light it or put it out |
| `goto` | `room` | move the player |
| `score` | `value` | add to score (negative works) |
| `set-counter` | `counter`, `value` | set a counter |
| `add-counter` | `counter`, `value` | add to a counter (negative subtracts) |
| `move-actor` | `actor`, `to` | move an actor |
| `win` | `text` or `pages[]` | end as a win. At least one must be reachable |
| `lose` | `text` or `pages[]` | end as a loss |

`pages` is the ending in beats rather than one wall of text, so it can be paced.

`chance` rolls off the world's own seeded generator: rolls differ within a run and
repeat exactly across runs, so a walkthrough that passed keeps passing. Do not gate
the only route to the ending on one.

### timers

Tick once per move, after the command's rule.

`turns` (required), `do` (required), plus `startFlag` (do not tick until true),
`stopFlag` (cancel when true), `if` (only tick while these hold), `repeat`,
`fuelFor` (publish elapsed as an item's fuel used, driving the lamp gauge).

A countdown the player can defeat needs `stopFlag`. Without one, a `lose` in a
timer is a cutscene rather than a hazard.

### internal flags

The engine keeps state in your flag namespace. Read them in conditions; do not
write them directly.

- `_open_<ITEM>` set by `open` / `close`
- `_lit_<ITEM>` set by `light` / `extinguish`
- `_fuelUsed_<ITEM>` maintained by a timer's `fuelFor`

### built-in verbs

The engine answers only: the twelve directions, `LOOK` (the room, or a thing if
you name one), `TAKE`, `DROP`, `OPEN` (refuses or reports; cannot actually open
anything), `INVENTORY`, and `WAIT`.

`WAIT` has no button. It exists for typing and for walkthroughs, so answer it if
you like but **never require it** to make progress.

**The player is shown eight verbs: `LOOK TAKE DROP OPEN CLOSE USE HIT SPEAK`.
Four of them (CLOSE, USE, HIT, SPEAK) do nothing without rules.** Assume every
verb needs writing, or half the buttons read as broken.

**Those eight, plus the compass and INVENTORY, are the ONLY verbs a player can
click.** A rule triggered by anything else (`UNLOCK`, `LIGHT`, `GIVE`, `DIG`) can
only be reached by opening the on-screen keyboard and typing it, which is the one
thing this engine exists to avoid. Validation warns with `W509`.

The idiom is to put custom actions on `USE`, which is deliberately vague so it can
carry them: `USE CELLAR-DOOR` to unlock, `USE LANTERN` to light, `USE DOG` to feed
it. Write for the buttons.

## Complete worked example

Three rooms, a locked door, a lamp that runs out, and a win. This validates.

```json
{
  "meta": {
    "title": "Cellar Door",
    "start": "PORCH",
    "defaults": {
      "blocked": "There is no way through.",
      "absent": "You don't see that here.",
      "dark": "It is pitch black. Something down here does not want to be seen.",
      "unknown": "Nothing happens."
    }
  },
  "flags": { "doorUnlocked": false },
  "rooms": [
    { "id": "PORCH", "name": "The Porch",
      "prose": "Paint curls off the boards. A cellar door lies flat against the ground.",
      "exits": [
        { "dir": "NORTH", "to": "HALL" },
        { "dir": "DOWN", "to": "CELLAR",
          "condition": { "type": "flag", "flag": "doorUnlocked" } }
      ] },
    { "id": "HALL", "name": "The Hall",
      "prose": "A narrow hall. A hook by the door holds nothing. A side table does.",
      "exits": [ { "dir": "SOUTH", "to": "PORCH" } ] },
    { "id": "CELLAR", "name": "The Cellar", "dark": true,
      "prose": "Earth floor, stone walls, and a smell like old coins.",
      "exits": [ { "dir": "UP", "to": "PORCH" } ] }
  ],
  "items": [
    { "id": "KEY", "name": "iron key", "location": "HALL",
      "roomProse": "An iron key lies on the side table.",
      "attributes": { "TAKEBIT": true } },
    { "id": "LANTERN", "name": "lantern", "location": "HALL",
      "roomProse": "A lantern hangs from the hook after all.",
      "attributes": { "TAKEBIT": true, "LIGHTSOURCE": true }, "fuel": 40 },
    { "id": "CELLAR-DOOR", "name": "cellar door", "location": "PORCH",
      "attributes": {} },
    { "id": "LOCKET", "name": "silver locket", "location": "CELLAR",
      "roomProse": "A silver locket lies half-buried in the earth.",
      "attributes": { "TAKEBIT": true } }
  ],
  "rules": [
    { "on": { "verb": "USE", "noun": "CELLAR-DOOR" },
      "if": [ { "type": "carrying", "item": "KEY" } ],
      "do": [
        { "type": "set-flag", "flag": "doorUnlocked", "value": true },
        { "type": "print", "text": "The key turns with a sound like a cough." },
        { "type": "score", "value": 5 }
      ] },
    { "on": { "verb": "USE", "noun": "CELLAR-DOOR" },
      "do": [ { "type": "print", "text": "It is locked, and you have nothing to turn." } ] },
    { "on": { "verb": "USE", "noun": "LANTERN" },
      "if": [ { "type": "carrying", "item": "LANTERN" } ],
      "do": [
        { "type": "light", "item": "LANTERN" },
        { "type": "print", "text": "The lantern catches, and the dark backs off a step." }
      ] },
    { "on": { "verb": "TAKE", "noun": "LOCKET" },
      "if": [
        { "type": "in-room", "item": "LOCKET" },
        { "type": "not", "condition": { "type": "flag", "flag": "_lit_LANTERN", "value": true } }
      ],
      "do": [ { "type": "print", "text": "You grope in the dark and find only cold earth." } ] },
    { "on": { "verb": "TAKE", "noun": "LOCKET" },
      "if": [ { "type": "in-room", "item": "LOCKET" } ],
      "do": [
        { "type": "take", "item": "LOCKET" },
        { "type": "score", "value": 10 },
        { "type": "win", "text": "*** You have won ***" }
      ] }
  ],
  "timers": [
    { "startFlag": "_lit_LANTERN", "fuelFor": "LANTERN", "turns": 40,
      "do": [
        { "type": "extinguish", "item": "LANTERN" },
        { "type": "print", "text": "The lantern gutters once and goes out." }
      ] }
  ]
}
```

Its walkthrough:

```
north
take key
take lantern
south
use cellar-door
use lantern
down
take locket
```

## The pictures

The engine draws the whole board except one pane: the scene, 144 by 104 pixels.
Everything else, the verb grid, the compass, the text pane, the inventory strip and
the status bar, is drawn for you and cannot be moved.

Scene code is real JavaScript and ships inside the container as
`presentation/scenes.js`:

```js
GUE.scenes = GUE.scenes || {};
GUE.scenes['PORCH'] = {
  // ctx is a 2D canvas already clipped to the pane; S is the state; t is a frame counter
  draw: function (ctx, S, t) { /* draw in 144x104 coordinates, never scale */ },
  // rectangles in the same space; obj is an item id, dir is a compass direction
  hotspots: function (S) {
    return [{ x: 44, y: 30, w: 56, h: 44, obj: 'HOUSE' },
            { x: 0, y: 44, w: 20, h: 30, dir: 'NORTH' }];
  }
};
```

A room with no scene renders a placeholder and the game is still playable, so art
is the last thing to do, not the first. Overlapping hotspots resolve smallest-first,
so a mailbox in front of a house wins. Full reference: https://folio.games/docs/scenes/

## What validation will tell you

It ends with one of four verdicts:

- `INVALID` — at least one error. It will not be hosted
- `VALID` — the manifest and integrity checks passed
- `PLAYABLE` — a path to the ending was proved by replaying your walkthrough
- `CERTIFIED` — every tier ran and the design audit raised nothing. The top tier

`PLAYABLE` and `CERTIFIED` both need a walkthrough that wins. Neither claims a
human could *find* the solution; that check does not exist yet.

Errors block; warnings are advice. Full list: https://folio.games/docs/errors/

The ones you will actually hit:

- `E212` your world violates the schema. The message names the exact path
- `E310` **the win state is not reachable**. The most common first failure.
  Either nothing declares a `win`, or a puzzle in the chain cannot be solved from
  the start. Work backwards from the win
- `E311` a room is unreachable. Usually a missing return exit
- `E410` the walkthrough ran out without winning. The hint says where it stopped
- `W500`–`W507` design opinions: too few rooms, shallow chains, a map with no
  loops, nothing that can kill you, keys sitting next to their locks

Thresholds come from measuring Zork I (82 rooms, 0.67 loops per room, 43% of
objects takeable, a reward about every 11.5 moves). If your game is deliberately
small or linear, ship `brief.json` and it is graded against your own intent:

```json
{ "length": "short", "difficulty": "gentle", "deadliness": "none",
  "sprawl": "balanced", "density": "sparse" }
```

Every dial and its legal values:

| dial | values |
|---|---|
| `length` | `short` \| `standard` \| `epic`, or `{"rooms": n}` |
| `difficulty` | `gentle` \| `standard` \| `cruel` |
| `deadliness` | `none` \| `fair` \| `classic` |
| `sprawl` | `linear` \| `balanced` \| `open` |
| `density` | `sparse` \| `balanced` \| `packed` |

An unrecognised value silently falls back to the middle setting rather than
erroring, so a typo costs you the dial without telling you.

## Writing advice that the validator cannot check

- Most of the world should be scenery. Zork keeps over half its objects as pure
  texture, and that is what makes the useful ones feel chosen. A world where
  everything matters reads as a shopping list. Writing a flavour response for a
  prop does **not** make it load-bearing; only being required by a condition, or
  changed by an effect, does. So write a verb for everything and still expect a
  large minority of your items to be mute.
- Failure branches are where the prose lives. A guarded rule with no fallback
  means the player who tries the right idea at the wrong time hears nothing.
- Distance makes a puzzle. A key in the same room as its lock is a formality.
- Counting is a counter, not a chain of near-identical rules. `add-counter` on
  each visit and `counter-equals` to branch is how you write "the third time".
- Foreshadow deaths. An unannounced instant death is an ambush, not a hazard.
